stem: Oscar is a 13-year-old boy with asthma. He uses terbutaline (Bricanyl) Turbuhaler when wheezy, but over the last few months he feels it has not been working during attacks. What is the first thing you should check to determine why Oscar’s medication might not be working?

options.text: Puffer is not out of medication or out of date
His technique when using the puffer
The number of puffs he is taking when needed
Timing of taking the medication relative to symptoms

explanation: The first step when a reliever seems ineffective is to check inhaler technique. Incorrect device use is a common reason for poor asthma medication delivery, especially with dry powder inhalers like a Turbuhaler.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

rationale: In asthma management, poor inhaler technique is a frequent cause of apparent treatment failure and should be checked before assuming the medication or dose is ineffective.

optionExplanations.A: Expiry or running out of medication can matter, but technique should be checked first.
optionExplanations.B: Correct inhaler technique is the most common and immediate issue to assess.
optionExplanations.C: Dose may need review, but first confirm the medication is being delivered properly.
optionExplanations.D: Timing can affect response, but it is not the first issue to check.
optionExplanations.E: Attack frequency helps assess control, but does not explain immediate lack of effect as directly as technique.
